description:
Security fix for issue #279: client-supplied X-Forwarded-For currently defeats every rate limit (API) and forges visitor identity (redirect). Root cause: both services set Fastify `trustProxy: true`, which makes req.ip the LEFTMOST (client-typed) X-Forwarded-For entry. Fix: add a shared, spoof-proof rightmost-XFF parser in @snapurl/domain that, given a configured number of trusted appending proxy hops, returns the (N+1)th-from-the-right XFF entry (falling back to the socket IP when there is no usable XFF), and wire it into BOTH services so the derived client IP is trustworthy. Then key @nestjs/throttler on that trustworthy IP via a custom getTracker, feed it to visitorHash in the redirect, and add per-route @Throttle limits tighter than the global on the three unauthenticated argon2 routes.

MECHANISM DECISION (verified during routing, cite in the PR summary): Fastify 5.11.3's numeric trustProxy hop-count is DISABLED and documented as unsafe (fastify.dev/docs/latest/Reference/Server -> trustProxy: 'Hop-count-only trust is disabled because it cannot validate the immediate peer and lets direct clients spoof X-Forwarded-* values'). So we do NOT rely on Fastify's numeric trustProxy. We implement the explicit rightmost-XFF parser (the issue's named 'portable fix'), which behaves identically in both services and in local dev. CloudFront APPENDS the viewer IP to the RIGHT of any client XFF (AWS docs, RequestAndResponseBehaviorCustomOrigin -> Client IP addresses), so attacker-prepended entries stay on the LEFT and the trustworthy entry is rightmost-minus-N.

SPOOF PROOF to encode in tests and reasoning: for header `X-Forwarded-For: <attacker>, <attacker2>, <realclient>, <edge1>...<edgeN>` with N trusted hops, the derived IP is the entry N positions from the right end = the real client. Any entries the attacker PREPENDS shift left and are ignored. With N=0 and no proxy, there is no trustworthy XFF entry, so the parser returns the socket IP (this is the local-dev / compose / verify-CI path, where services are hit directly on localhost with no XFF, keeping smoke green).
steps: Add a new pure module packages/domain/src/client-ip.ts exporting a function, e.g. `clientIpFromXff(opts: { xff: string | string[] | undefined; socketIp: string; trustedHops: number }): string`. Behavior: normalise xff to a single comma-joined string (Fastify may pass an array or a comma string; handle both); split on commas; trim each entry; drop empty entries; if trustedHops <= 0 OR there are not enough entries to index (entries.length <= trustedHops), return socketIp; otherwise return entries[entries.length - 1 - trustedHops] (the (N+1)th from the right). Guard malformed input: if the chosen entry is empty/whitespace, fall back to socketIp. Do NOT do strict IP validation beyond trimming/non-empty (keep it portable and IPv6-safe: entries may be IPv6 like 2001:db8::1). Document the CloudFront-appends-rightmost rationale and the spoof-proof property in a doc comment.
Export the new module from packages/domain/src/index.ts (add `export * from "./client-ip.js";`).

Add packages/domain/src/client-ip.test.ts (vitest) covering: (a) attacker-prepended entries are ignored for hops=1 and hops=2 given a realistic CloudFront chain e.g. xff='1.1.1.1, 2.2.2.2, 203.0.113.9, 198.51.100.1' -> hops=1 returns 203.0.113.9, hops=2 returns 2.2.2.2 (demonstrating N selects rightmost-minus-N); (b) hops=0 returns the socket IP even when an XFF is present (local/direct path); (c) no XFF header returns the socket IP; (d) empty/whitespace-only XFF returns the socket IP; (e) hops exceeding the number of entries returns the socket IP; (f) an IPv6 entry is returned intact; (g) array-form xff (Fastify multi-header) is handled. Add an explicit test asserting that a client PREPENDING extra entries to a fixed real chain does NOT change the derived IP.

apps/api config: in apps/api/src/config/env.ts add `TRUSTED_PROXY_HOPS: z.coerce.number().int().min(0).default(0)` to EnvSchema with a doc comment: 0 = direct/local dev and compose (no trusted appending proxy); production sets it to the count of proxies that APPEND to X-Forwarded-For in front of this service (e.g. CloudFront=1; CloudFront + API Gateway HTTP API v2 that appends = 2; tune to the actual deployment topology).

apps/api throttler: create a subclass of ThrottlerGuard (e.g. apps/api/src/common/proxy-aware-throttler.guard.ts) that overrides `protected async getTracker(req)` to return clientIpFromXff({ xff: req.headers['x-forwarded-for'], socketIp: req.socket?.remoteAddress ?? req.ip, trustedHops: <TRUSTED_PROXY_HOPS> }). Inject the hop count: since APP_GUARD useClass cannot easily read env, either (i) register the guard with useFactorywaitFactory-style via a provider that injects ENV and constructs the guard, or (ii) read the hop count through Nest DI by making the subclass @Injectable and injecting ENV, keeping the ThrottlerGuard constructor args. Prefer approach (ii): @Injectable() class ProxyAwareThrottlerGuard extends ThrottlerGuard, add ENV to its constructor via @Inject(ENV), and pass the base ThrottlerModuleOptions/storage/reflector through. Then in apps/api/src/app.module.ts change the APP_GUARD registration from `useClass: ThrottlerGuard` to `useClass: ProxyAwareThrottlerGuard`. Confirm req.socket.remoteAddress is available under @nestjs/platform-fastify (Fastify raw request); if not, fall back to Fastify's request.ip. Do NOT remove the ThrottlerGuard APP_GUARD entry order relative to AuthGuard.

apps/api main.ts: keep FastifyAdapter but change `trustProxy: true`. Because the throttler now derives the IP itself and Fastify numeric hop-count is disabled, set trustProxy to false (do not blindly trust any proxy for req.ip), OR trust only loopback/private CIDR if that is needed for local logging. Choose `trustProxy: false` unless the app relies on request.ip elsewhere; grep apps/api/src for other request.ip / req.ip uses first and note the decision. The authoritative client IP for throttling comes from the custom getTracker, not from Fastify's req.ip.

apps/api per-route throttles: add `@Throttle({ default: { limit: 5, ttl: 60_000 } })` to the three named argon2 routes, mirroring the decorator shape at public.controller.ts:65. Routes: apps/api/src/auth/auth.controller.ts login (@Post('login')), apps/api/src/auth/auth.controller.ts 2fa/verify (@Post('2fa/verify')), apps/api/src/public/public.controller.ts unlock (@Post('links/:slug/unlock')). Import Throttle from '@nestjs/throttler' in auth.controller.ts (public.controller.ts already imports it). Rationale to put in a comment on each: 5/min per IP is far tighter than the global 120/min, blunts argon2id (19 MiB) CPU-burn and email-enumeration on login while staying usable for a human who fat-fingers a password a couple of times (5 attempts/min is generous for a person, punishing for a script). Use 5 for login and unlock; 5 for 2fa/verify as well (2fa/verify loops argon2 over every unused recovery code, so it is the most expensive per call). If you judge login should be slightly more forgiving, 5 is defensible and consistent; keep all three at 5 unless you document a reason to differ. Do NOT throttle register unless trivially consistent; the three named are the requirement.

apps/redirect main.ts: change `Fastify({ ..., trustProxy: true })`. Set trustProxy to false (Fastify's request.ip will then be the socket IP; we derive the real client IP ourselves). Add a TRUSTED_PROXY_HOPS read near the other env reads: `const TRUSTED_PROXY_HOPS = Number(process.env.TRUSTED_PROXY_HOPS ?? 0);` (plain env read, consistent with the other process.env reads in this file). At both call sites where visitorHash is computed (the handler ~line 131 and inside record() ~line 239), replace `ip: request.ip` with `ip: clientIpFromXff({ xff: request.headers['x-forwarded-for'], socketIp: request.raw.socket.remoteAddress ?? request.ip, trustedHops: TRUSTED_PROXY_HOPS })`. Import clientIpFromXff from '@snapurl/domain'. NOTE: record() currently receives a narrow `request: { ip: string; headers: Record<string,unknown> }` param type; widen that param type so it also carries what the parser needs (the x-forwarded-for header via headers, and a socket ip). Simplest: compute the client IP once in the handler and pass it into record() as a parameter (e.g. add a clientIp arg), rather than re-deriving inside record(). Ensure the precomputedHash path already used in the handler still short-circuits so the hash is computed once. Confirm the record() signature change compiles and the blocked-click record() call (which passes request directly) also supplies the derived clientIp.

Document the env in apps/api/.env.example: add a TRUSTED_PROXY_HOPS entry with a comment (default 0 for local/compose/direct; set to the number of X-Forwarded-For-APPENDING proxies in front of the API in production, e.g. CloudFront=1). Place it near the THROTTLE_* block.

Document the env in apps/redirect/.env.example: add TRUSTED_PROXY_HOPS with a comment (default 0 for local dev and compose where the service is hit directly; production sets it to the number of appending proxies, e.g. behind CloudFront=1).

Do NOT add TRUSTED_PROXY_HOPS to docker-compose.yml (compose hits services directly with no XFF, so the default 0 is correct there and keeps the compose integration + verify smoke jobs green). If you add it to compose for documentation, it MUST be 0.
Grep the redirect and api sources for any other consumers of request.ip / req.ip to ensure none silently regress (e.g. logging). Note findings.
acceptance_criteria: packages/domain exports clientIpFromXff and its unit test passes: attacker-prepended entries never change the derived IP; hops 0/1/2 select the correct entry (rightmost-minus-N); no/empty/short/IPv6/array XFF all handled; hops=0 with a present XFF returns the socket IP.
apps/api uses a ProxyAwareThrottlerGuard whose getTracker returns clientIpFromXff(...); a rotating X-Forwarded-For no longer changes the throttle key, so it can no longer reset any limit.
TRUSTED_PROXY_HOPS is in the apps/api zod EnvSchema (default 0) and in both .env.example files with explanatory comments.

Both main.ts files no longer pass trustProxy: true; the redirect derives visitorHash's ip via clientIpFromXff at both hash sites (computed once and shared), so a client-supplied header cannot influence visitorHash.
The three argon2 routes (login, 2fa/verify, unlock) carry @Throttle limits tighter than the global THROTTLE_LIMIT (120), using the same decorator shape as the forms route.
corepack pnpm type-check passes; corepack pnpm test passes (DB-gated tests still skip in-sandbox); the build succeeds.
The default hop count (0) keeps scripts/smoke-redirect.sh, the compose integration job, and the verify job green because those hit services directly with no XFF (socket-IP fallback).
verification: export PATH="/opt/toolchains/.nvm/versions/node/v22.23.2/bin:$PATH" && rm -rf web/.next && NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL=https://api.example.com/api/v1 corepack pnpm build
findings:
Implemented as specified. New pure module packages/domain/src/client-ip.ts exports clientIpFromXff (rightmost-minus-N XFF parser, socket fallback, IPv6/array/empty handling) with 9 unit tests in client-ip.test.ts (all pass, incl. explicit spoof-proof prepend test). Exported via domain barrel.

Grep for req.ip/request.ip consumers: the ONLY consumers were the two visitorHash sites in apps/redirect/src/main.ts (handler ~131 and inside record() ~239). apps/api had no direct req.ip/request.ip use outside @nestjs/throttler's internal getTracker default. So setting trustProxy:false in both main.ts files is safe.

apps/api: added TRUSTED_PROXY_HOPS to zod EnvSchema (z.coerce.number().int().min(0).default(0)). Created ProxyAwareThrottlerGuard (apps/api/src/common/proxy-aware-throttler.guard.ts): @Injectable subclass of ThrottlerGuard, injects ENV via @Inject, passes base (options, storageService, reflector) through to super; overrides getTracker to return clientIpFromXff({ xff: req.headers['x-forwarded-for'], socketIp: req.raw?.socket?.remoteAddress ?? req.ip, trustedHops: env.TRUSTED_PROXY_HOPS }). Under @nestjs/platform-fastify the guard receives the Fastify request, so req.raw.socket.remoteAddress is the peer and req.ip is the safe fallback. Swapped APP_GUARD useClass ThrottlerGuard -> ProxyAwareThrottlerGuard, keeping order after AuthGuard. main.ts FastifyAdapter now trustProxy:false.

Per-route @Throttle({ default: { limit: 5, ttl: 60_000 } }) added to login, 2fa/verify (auth.controller.ts, added Throttle import) and unlock (public.controller.ts), mirroring the forms route decorator shape. 5/min is tighter than the global 120/min.

apps/redirect: trustProxy:false; added const TRUSTED_PROXY_HOPS = Number(process.env.TRUSTED_PROXY_HOPS ?? 0). Compute the trustworthy clientIp ONCE in the handler and thread it through both the handler visitorHash and both record() calls. Widened record()'s param: replaced the narrow { ip; headers } request param with a clientIp:string arg plus { headers } (headers still needed for country/city/referer). Both call sites (blocked path + success path) updated; precomputedHash short-circuit preserved so the hash is computed once on the success path.

Env documented in both .env.example files (default 0, comments). docker-compose.yml intentionally NOT touched (compose hits services directly with no XFF; default 0 keeps smoke/compose/verify green).

Verification: corepack pnpm --filter @snapurl/domain test (122 pass), corepack pnpm type-check (all packages pass), corepack pnpm test (full suite pass; DB-gated integration tests skip in-sandbox as expected), and the web build all succeed.
